This page lists every known error in the published reviews, with the date it was found and what was changed. Corrections are inserted into the affected review as dated notes; the original sentence is left in place so readers can see what was wrong. The round-two Claude syntheses also carry a Verification notes section in which the overseer model tagged each checked sub-review claim as CONFIRMED, CORRECTED or COULD NOT CHECK; across the 13 round-two papers, 14 of 264 checked claims were corrected at that stage. Those in-pipeline corrections are visible in each synthesis and are not repeated here.

| Date | Paper | Reader | Where | What was wrong | Correction |
|----------|------------------|-------|--------------------|-------------------------|------------------------------|
| 2026-09-25 | [Odle, Duke & Dunens](papers/P07_odle/index.qmd) (AERA Open) | [Claude](papers/P07_odle/claude.qmd) | Synthesis, Key Concerns (access bullet); same text in the full Claude review | Said the paper's text never mentions the Pell Ratio row of Table 3. | Pages 10 and 11 discuss it. What the prose does not connect to the access claim is Table 1's descriptive Pell Ratio and Pell share. The critique of the abstract's access claim stands. |
| 2026-09-25 | [Umansky, Avelar & Thompson](papers/P12_umansky/index.qmd) (AERJ) | [Claude](papers/P12_umansky/claude.qmd) | Synthesis, Key Concerns and What to Treat Cautiously; same text in the full Claude review, plus the Writing sub-review | Said Tables 3 and 8 carry no significance legend. | All five tables have legends. The paper uses four distinct legend schemes, so one asterisk denotes three different thresholds across tables. The advice to read each table's note stands. |
| 2026-09-25 | [Little, Drake, White & Rowan](papers/P13_little/index.qmd) (AERJ) | [Claude](papers/P13_little/claude.qmd) | Synthesis, Key Strengths and What to Rely On; same text in the full Claude review | Presented the gap between general and strategic support as robust and said support "far outruns" Pre-K's standing as a strategic priority, without noting what Figure 4 shows. | Figure 4 (p. 16) shows 79% agree or strongly agree that early childhood education is among the district's top three strategic initiatives. The strongly-agree contrast (83% vs 38%) is real; a general absence of strategic priority is not shown. |
| 2026-09-25 | [Camp, Anglum, Koedel et al.](papers/P20_camp/index.qmd) (EEPA) | [Codex](papers/P20_camp/codex.qmd) | Synthesis, Key Concerns and Verification notes; Writing sub-review | Said Figure 3's vertical axis reads "Change in Teacher Retention." | On the rendered page (p. 15) it reads "Change in Teacher Recruitment." The parallel observation about Figure 2 (p. 13) is correct. |

## Per-paper notes

- [Xu, Flanagan & Quintero](papers/P15_xu/index.qmd) (EEPA): The PDF reviewed was typeset 2026-07-17, before the corrigendum published 2026-08-07 (doi 10.3102/01623737261473601). The corrigendum adds an author acknowledgment and changes no results.
- [Cleveland & Lukes](papers/P22_cleveland/index.qmd) (EEPA): As of 2026-09-25, Crossref lists no correction or corrigendum for this article. The review's central finding about Figure 3 should be re-checked against the journal's current version before being relied on.

To report an error, open an issue in the site's GitHub repository or use the discussion thread on the paper's page.
